<content>
{"subject": "Flow Step Output", "description": "TypeScript implementation types and handler contracts for the Exaix request/plan REST interface", "steps": [{"step": 1, "title": "Core domain types", "description": "```typescript
type RequestStatus =
  | "queued"
  | "planning"
  | "running"
  | "cancelling"
  | "succeeded"
  | "failed"
  | "cancelled";

const TERMINAL_STATUSES: ReadonlySet<RequestStatus> = new Set([
  "succeeded", "failed", "cancelled",
]);

interface RequestProgress {
  percent: number;
  currentStep: string | null;
  totalSteps: number;
}

interface ExaixRequest {
  id: string;
  tenantId: string;
  status: RequestStatus;
  input: Record<string, unknown>;
  result: Record<string, unknown> | null;
  error: { code: string; message: string } | null;
  planId: string | null;
  progress: RequestProgress | null;
  createdAt: string;
  updatedAt: string;
}

type PlanStepStatus = "pending" | "running" | "succeeded" | "failed" | "skipped";

interface PlanStep {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  status: PlanStepStatus;
  startedAt: string | null;
  finishedAt: string | null;
}

interface Plan {
  id: string;
  version: number;
  requestId: string;
  steps: PlanStep[];
  createdAt: string;
}
```
All seven `RequestStatus` values and the terminal set are defined once and imported everywhere — the transition table and the CAS writes in step 3 both reference `TERMINAL_STATUSES` rather than re-deriving it, so the invariant ("terminal states accept no further transitions") can never drift out of sync between the two call sites."}, {"step": 2, "title": "Error hierarchy matching the retryable contract", "description": "```typescript
class AppError extends Error {
  constructor(
    message: string,
    public code: string,
    public statusCode: number,
    public retryable: boolean,
  ) {
    super(message);
    this.name = this.constructor.name;
  }

  toBody(): { error: { code: string; message: string; retryable: boolean } } {
    return { error: { code: this.code, message: this.message, retryable: this.retryable } };
  }
}

class ValidationError extends AppError {
  constructor(message: string, public field?: string) {
    super(message, "VALIDATION_ERROR", 400, false);
  }
}

class UnauthorizedError extends AppError {
  constructor() { super("Authentication required", "UNAUTHORIZED", 401, false); }
}

class NotFoundError extends AppError {
  constructor() { super("Resource not found", "NOT_FOUND", 404, false); }
}

class ConflictError extends AppError {
  constructor(message: string) { super(message, "CONFLICT", 409, false); }
}

class RateLimitedError extends AppError {
  constructor(public retryAfterSeconds: number) {
    super("Rate limit exceeded", "RATE_LIMITED", 429, true);
  }
}

class InternalError extends AppError {
  constructor() { super("Internal server error", "INTERNAL_ERROR", 500, true); }
}
```
Every `AppError` subclass carries `retryable` at construction time and serializes it via `toBody()`, so the error contract the PM specified (`{error: {code, message, retryable}}`) is enforced by the type system rather than by convention — a handler cannot emit a malformed error body. `NotFoundError`'s message is fixed and generic (per the architect's tenant-scoping note: cross-tenant access returns 404, never a message that reveals the resource existed), so no call site can accidentally leak resource details into it."}, {"step": 3, "title": "Atomic status transition + cancel idempotency", "description": "```typescript
interface StatusStore {
  casTransition(
    requestId: string,
    tenantId: string,
    from: RequestStatus[],
    to: RequestStatus,
  ): Promise<boolean>; // true iff this call performed the transition
}

async function cancelRequest(
  store: StatusStore,
  requestId: string,
  tenantId: string,
  current: ExaixRequest,
): Promise<{ status: RequestStatus }> {
  if (TERMINAL_STATUSES.has(current.status)) {
    throw new ConflictError(`Request is already ${current.status}`);
  }
  if (current.status === "cancelling") {
    return { status: "cancelling" }; // idempotent no-op, per architect step 3
  }
  if (current.status === "queued") {
    const applied = await store.casTransition(requestId, tenantId, ["queued"], "cancelled");
    return { status: applied ? "cancelled" : current.status };
  }
  await store.casTransition(requestId, tenantId, ["planning", "running"], "cancelling");
  return { status: "cancelling" };
}

// Executor-side race resolution, called from two independent completion paths:
async function completeRequest(store: StatusStore, requestId: string, tenantId: string): Promise<void> {
  await store.casTransition(requestId, tenantId, ["running", "cancelling"], "succeeded");
}
async function finishCancellation(store: StatusStore, requestId: string, tenantId: string): Promise<void> {
  await store.casTransition(requestId, tenantId, ["cancelling"], "cancelled");
}
```
`casTransition` is the single choke point for every state write; its `from` array is exactly the set of legal predecessor states per the architect's transition table, so an out-of-order or duplicate executor event (retried delivery) simply returns `false` and is dropped rather than corrupting state — this is the compare-and-swap the architect specified, expressed as one reusable primitive instead of ad-hoc `UPDATE ... WHERE` calls scattered across handlers."}, {"step": 4, "title": "SSE handler with Last-Event-ID resume", "description": "```typescript
interface SseEvent {
  seq: number;
  event: "status" | "progress" | "step" | "resync";
  data: ExaixRequest;
}

interface EventBuffer {
  since(requestId: string, afterSeq: number): SseEvent[] | null; // null = rolled off, caller must resync
}

async function streamRequestEvents(
  requestId: string,
  tenantId: string,
  lastEventId: string | null,
  buffer: EventBuffer,
  fetchCurrent: () => Promise<ExaixRequest>,
  write: (event: SseEvent) => void,
): Promise<void> {
  if (lastEventId !== null) {
    const afterSeq = Number.parseInt(lastEventId, 10);
    if (Number.isNaN(afterSeq)) throw new ValidationError("Invalid Last-Event-ID");
    const backlog = buffer.since(requestId, afterSeq);
    if (backlog === null) {
      const current = await fetchCurrent();
      write({ seq: afterSeq, event: "resync", data: current });
    } else {
      for (const evt of backlog) write(evt);
    }
  }
  // subscribe to live events from here; loop terminates after a terminal-state event
}
```
The `since` → `null` branch is the architect's rolled-buffer case: rather than silently resuming from a stale point, it forces a `resync` event carrying a full `ExaixRequest` snapshot (identical shape to `GET /requests/{id}`), so client-side state reducers can reuse the same reducer for both the initial GET and any SSE `resync` event instead of needing separate merge logic."}]}
</content>
